items.title: Vendor SDE methodology, Visual Engineering context, and WASM kernel dependency
Attribute pre-ROS setup artifacts (kernel dep, VE context, SDE)
Record and resolve CI deviation: ./ros F# launcher unusable, CI runs Node ros_cli.mjs
items.description: AGENTS.md (GV-START-001 v1.3.0, section 'F# CLI') states Node is no longer a CLI anywhere in this project or what it scaffolds, and that tools/ros_cli.mjs is no longer characterized or scaffolded as a CLI rollback path. .github/workflows/ros-validation.yml currently invokes 'node tools/ros_cli.mjs' for both steps, contradicting that contract. The change was forced: ros.json pins rosVersion 2.0.1-main.78.1, and the ./ros launcher 404s obtaining that tag's release assets (checksums.txt and ros-fs-linux-x64 are both absent upstream, while v2.0.1 publishes them), so ./ros cannot execute and the scaffolded workflow failed on every run. Requirement Set 0 sections 0.1 and 0.1.1 make ROS adherence mandatory and forbid deviation, so this is recorded rather than left silent. Consequences: CI no longer exercises the canonical binary, so F#/Node behavioural divergence is invisible; ros-bootstrap verify reports one managed-file drift finding on the workflow while the patch stands. Migration: publish release assets for v2.0.1-main.78.1 upstream in kemiller2002/repository-operating-system, verify ./ros runs, revert the workflow to ./ros, confirm ros-bootstrap verify is clean, then supersede or withdraw the decision record. Full analysis, evidence, alternatives considered, and verification results are in research/decisions/DF-SUMMA-ROSCLI-2026-0001--ci-uses-node-ros-cli-instead-of-fsharp-launcher.md. Note: this work item was itself created through the Node CLI because ./ros is unavailable.

items.title: Summa 01: publish the Chrona-to-Summa contract as a small versioned contracts package (pure F# types and JSON codec), released through Summa's release workflow and registered in echelon-registry
items.description: User decision 2026-10-08: the application that ACCEPTS the data owns the contract, so Summa owns the Chrona-to-Summa contract. Build order is Chrona first, then Summa; this item is pulled forward because Chrona's integration item consumes it. A separate packable project (for example EchelonFoundry.Summa.Contracts): pure F# types for the publishable time projection (source application, source id and revision, organization, project, exact and billable minutes, policy id and version, publication id) and the feedback messages (InvoicedExternally, AdjustmentRequired), plus a canonical JSON codec with explicit contract version and golden vectors. No dependency on Summa internals. Release it through Summa's release workflow with the nuget-library release contract, and add it to echelon-registry so Chrona pins it through conditor.json. Requirements: SUM0-024, SUM0-025, SUM0-026, SUM1-017, SUM2-031, INV-CHR, INV-CONTRACT, INV-SOURCE; Chrona CHX-170, CHX-180. Also INV-PROV-003 and INV-PROV-008 (docs/requirements/SUMMA-PROVENANCE.md): each published source carries its origin verbatim, explicitly unknown when absent, never a credential.

items.title: Summa 02: configurable data location, Summa-owned namespace, application and organization manifests (SUM-DATALOC-001, SUM0-005..011, SUM0-033, SUM0-043)
items.description: Depends on arca slice 2 (data location, ARCA-LOC) and arca slice 3 (record format, ARCA-REC). New requirement SUM-DATALOC-001 (docs/requirements/SUMMA-DATA-LOCATION.md, user decision 2026-10-08): the data repository is configured per deployment, never hard-coded; Summa creates and owns its namespace (apps/summa/...) and never assumes it is alone in the repository; Summa's financial data must be separable under different permissions from other applications such as Chrona, which means its own repository, because GitHub permissions are per repository; no at-rest encryption for now. Plus app.json, organization.json, organization isolation and storage location (repository, base path, organization path), deterministic discovery and path safety.

items.title: Summa 03: GitHub sign-in through Fides, token handling, principals and capability authorization (SUM0-003, SUM0-004, SUM0-022, SUM0-023, SUM2-029, SUM3-012..015)
items.description: Depends on fides slice 7 (WASM client and Arca token provider, FID-CLI) and arca slice 5 (token-provider port, ARCA-AUTH). Sign in through Fides. Tokens never reach files, records, logs, exports or audit. Human/Agent/Service principals with actor identity on every command, and agent actions never recorded as human. Capability-based Summa authorization separate from GitHub authentication. Human approval boundaries. Also INV-PROV-006 (docs/requirements/SUMMA-PROVENANCE.md): identity is provenance, not authority.

items.title: Summa 04: authoritative financial storage on Arca - one record per file, command-to-commit, optimistic concurrency, no silent rebase (SUM0-002, SUM0-012..021, SUM0-027, SUM0-028, SUM0-044..046, SUM3-001, SUM3-003, SUM3-005, SUM0-034, SUM1-019 remainder)
items.description: Depends on WI-0018, WI-0019, arca slice 6 (GitHub adapter, ARCA-API/OUT) and arca slice 8 (integrity, ARCA-INT). Persist the Summa.Ledger, invoice and payment records through Arca as canonical JSON, one financial object or event per file at deterministic paths. One financial command is one commit (for example 'summa: issue invoice INV-2026-0042'). Commands carry the expected repository state; when HEAD moves they are revalidated, never silently rebased. Draft records are mutable and posted ones immutable. Corrections are compensating records. No physical deletion of financial records. Git history is evidence only. Storage avoids the scale traps of SUM0-034, and idempotency (SUM1-019) extends to storage retries through Arca idempotency keys. Also the WI-0018 remainders, applied to every financial write against GitHub: SUM0-005..009, SUM0-011 and SUM0-043 (Summa.Storage namespaces, application and organization manifests). Also the WI-0019 remainders: every financial command authorizes through Summa.Access (capability and approval gate) before it commits, and carries and records its Actor (SUM0-023, SUM3-013, SUM3-014).

items.title: Summa 05: integrity and tamper detection, schema versioning and migration safety, integrity before availability (SUM0-029..032, SUM0-047, SUM3-004, SUM3-009, SUM3-010, SUM3-019)
items.description: Depends on WI-0020. Validate manually modified data (schema, identity, references, accounting invariants, hashes, organization boundaries, version). Detect modification of posted records. Explicit versioned migrations that preserve financial meaning. Refuse a command when state cannot be proven valid. Monitor invariant violations.

items.title: Summa 06: rebuildable runtime index, reconciliation jobs, failure recovery, backup and restore drills (SUM0-014, SUM0-015, SUM3-002, SUM3-006..008, SUM3-020, SUM3-044)
items.description: Depends on WI-0020 and arca slice 10 (derived indexes and migration, ARCA-MIG). Projections (trial balance, AR aging, dashboards, search) are rebuildable and never authoritative. Stale projections are detected. Reconciliation jobs, encrypted backups (SUM3-024: transport and backups encrypted; application-level at-rest encryption is deferred by user decision 2026-10-08, and the repository is protected by repository permissions), restore testing, recovery objectives and drills. Also SUM0-034 remainder: a command reads the whole organization folder today; the rebuildable index removes that scale trap. Also the WI-0021 remainders: run financial migrations through Arca migration with Verification.checkMigration before activating (SUM0-032, SUM3-010).

items.title: Summa 12: audit provenance, audit immutability and agent execution safety (SUM1-018, SUM2-028, SUM2-030, SUM3-021, INV-AUD, INV-AGENT, SUM4-042..045, SUM0-048, SUM0-049)
items.description: Depends on WI-0019 and WI-0020. Audit events are immutable records with actor kind, execution id and correlation id. Agents use domain commands only, with explanation, human override and no autonomous financial surprises. Agents never edit authoritative files directly (SUM0-048) and read only the context they need (SUM0-049). Also INV-PROV-001, INV-PROV-002, INV-PROV-006, INV-PROV-007 and INV-PROV-008 (docs/requirements/SUMMA-PROVENANCE.md): Praxis-compatible actors, opaque execution ids, both contributions kept when a human changes an agent proposal. Also SUM0-023 and SUM3-014 remainders: audit events carry the full Summa.Access Actor (kind, agent identity, execution and correlation), not only the actor id the ledger records today.

items.title: Summa 03b: sign in with GitHub through Fides 0.2.0 in the application - Identity port over Limen requests, session actor github:<id>, token provider to Arca, never a token in state (SUM0-003, SUM0-004, SUM3-012)
items.description: Follows WI-0019 (domain: principals, capabilities, approval gates, rosters, bootstrap administrators). Copy Chrona WI-0029 (DF-CHRONA-2026-0004): run Fides' own client inside the Limen request/reply loop (exchange over Http, device/tab storage, leave for GitHub, address-bar tidy, cross-tab messages); the actor is github:<numeric subject>, the login only a display name; Arca gets Fides.Arca's token provider, never a token; sign-in states and retention in the engine; SignInTests run the real Fides client against a fake exchange. Anonymous financial mutation impossible (SUM3-012); tokens never in files, records, logs, exports or audit (SUM0-004). Needs the application shell; may land with WI-0030's first page.

items.title: Real end-to-end sign-in and storage check against the user's Fides deployment and a Summa data repository
items.description: Blocked on the user's deployment: no AWS account, domain or GitHub App exists yet, so Fides is deployed nowhere. When it exists: put the exchange origin, application id, GitHub App client id and redirect URI in summa.deployment.json (docs/deployment-configuration.md), point location at a private Summa data repository, list a bootstrap administrator's GitHub numeric id, then sign in, found the organization, issue an invoice, record a payment, sign out, and confirm every commit landed in <basePath>/summa with no token anywhere in the repository. Until then all tests use Arca's in-memory provider and fake Fides exchanges. Also SUM3-044: run the recovery drill (docs/operations/recovery.md) once against the production-like deployment before real books are trusted to Summa. Also SUM0-039: stand up a synthetic staging environment that exercises storage, sign-in, commands, concurrency, migrations, invoices, payments, reports and backup.

items.title: Summa 04b: the application's store on GitHub - Arca's GitHub provider with the Fides token provider, start-up from the manifests, the offline queue on localStorage and conflict resolution in the interface (SUM0-002, SUM0-007, SUM0-018, SUM0-019)
items.description: Follows WI-0020 (provider-neutral command-to-commit in Summa.Storage.Commands) and WI-0035 (sign-in). Copy Chrona WI-0032/WI-0033/WI-0035: the application's store port runs Summa.Storage.Commands.execute over GitHubStorage.provider (Limen Http effects, Fides.Arca token provider, never a token), opens Summa's and the organization's namespaces through their manifests on start-up (SUM0-007, SUM0-033) and refuses a public production repository; financial commands commit directly to the configured data branch (SUM0-018) while schema and storage-format changes stay in reviewed code (SUM0-019, Arca migrations); offline writes queue on localStorage through Arca's OfflineQueue (OfflinePolicy.QueueWrites) and are sent in order on reconnect, a blocked entry reloaded, revalidated and revised or abandoned; conflicts and outside edits are shown, never resolved silently. Proven against Arca's fake GitHub and in a browser suite. Also SUM3-009 remainder: start-up checks Compatibility.access and fails safely when the data is incompatible. Also SUM3-038 remainder: drain or persist the offline queue before shutdown so no operation is left halfway. Remainder after WI-0027: drafts survive refresh, navigation, connection loss and session interruption through the offline queue (INV-DRAFT-003).

items.title: Summa 06b: financial schema migrations - run a record-schema change as an explicit, versioned migration through Arca, checked by Verification.checkMigration before it is activated (SUM0-032, SUM3-010)
items.description: WI-0021 built the safety checks (identity or lineage, trial balance unless a declared correction, invariants after) and WI-0022 the backup and restore. This item runs a migration end to end: open the folder read-only, transform the books, check, write the new schema versions and the manifest's recordSchemas through Arca's Migration (validate, copy, verify, activate, retire), with a backup taken first and the reconciliation run before and after. Also SUM3-039: every migration states its rollback before it runs (keep the pre-migration backup and the old schema readable until the new one is verified).

items.title: Summa 14b: GitHub Pages deployment of the accounting app on summa.echelonfoundry.com (after WI-0030)
items.description: Depends on WI-0030: do this once the accounting app has a browser page that works without the local Node server. Copy the pattern of chrona#55 and signal#36: a GitHub Pages workflow; a deploy/pages/ folder holding the Pages configuration; a demo banner on the deployed page; and a Content-Security-Policy meta tag. Pages is already enabled for kemiller2002/summa on the custom domain summa.echelonfoundry.com. Deploy only the static accounting app: the backlog and hub tools need /api/* and must not be deployed. Same rules as every change: a PR, every check green on the exact head SHA before merging.

items.title: Summa 11b: explicit tax model room (INV-ADJ-005)
items.description: Remainder of INV-ADJ after WI-0027. Tax calculation stays deferred, but the model must leave room for taxable and non-taxable lines, tax category or code, customer tax-exempt status, jurisdiction, tax rate source, tax amount, tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive pricing, and tax evidence or reference. Summa must not infer tax obligations from incomplete data. WI-0027 already supports an explicit Tax adjustment posted to a named liability account.
